texts.preamble: Manohar Lal & Anr vs State & Anr on 17 May, 2017 Author: Pushpendra Singh Bhati Bench: Pushpendra Singh Bhati High Court Of Judicature For Rajasthan At Jodhpur S.B. Criminal Misc(Pet.) No. 1826 / 2013 1. Manohar Lal S/o Mangi Lal 2. Dharmendra S/o Manohar Lal Both petitioners by caste Mali, residents of In front of Rajmahal Birla School, Jodhpur. ----Petitioners Versus 1. State of Rajasthan. 2. Ramdayal Sankhala S/o Mangi Lal Sankhala, by caste Mali, resident of Behind Namdeo School, Sunthala, Jodhpur. ----Respondents Connected With S.B. Criminal Misc(Pet.) No. 1951 / 2014 1. Manohar Lal S/o Mangi Lal 2. Dharmendra Sankhala S/o Manohar Lal Both by caste Mali, residents of Rajmahal, Opp. B.R. Birla School, R.K. Nagar, Jodhpur. ----Petitioners Versus 1. State of Rajasthan. 2. Ram Dayal S/o Mangi Lal, by caste Mali, resident of Behind Namdev School, Sunthla, Jodhpur. ----Respondents _____________________________________________________ For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Sunil Beniwal For Respondent(s) : Mr. V.S. Rajpurohit, Pp Mr. Rampal Singh _____________________________________________________ Hon'Ble Dr. Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati Judgment 17/05/2017 1.
texts.facts: The petitioners have preferred this Criminal Misc. (2 of 5) [ CRLMP-1826/2013] Petition No.1826/2013 under Section 482 Cr.P.C. for quashing of FIR Nos.400/2013 & 203/2014 registered at Police Station Pratapnagar, Jodhpur for the offences under Sections 420, 448, 452, 379, 406, 467, 468, 471 & 120-B of IPC and Section 63 of Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006. Manohar Lal & Anr vs State & Anr on 17 May, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85021612/ 1 2. The respondent No.2 in fact lodged a complaint in which FIR No.400/2013 was lodged at Police Station Pratapnagar, Jodhpur against the petitioner No.1 who is real brother of the complainant and also against his nephew who is petitioner No.2. The allegations were that Plot No.34D in Pratapnagar, Jodhpur, an industry namely M/s. Ganesh & Sons was set up and while the petitioner No.1 was working as a helper, he prepared a forged Bakshishnama on forged signatures which enabled him to get patta issued in his favour. The allegation also included effort by the petitioner to grab the machinery in the workshop and also stealing of the bill books. Upon the final report being lodged by the prosecution, the same was challenged before the competent court vide order dated 07.01.2009 after taking the statements of the complainant, the learned court below took the cognizance. Thus, the petitioner has sought quashing of the FIR and the proceedings initiated thereto. 3. The brief facts of criminal misc. petition No. 1951/2014 as noticed by this Court are that the complaint was regarding a particular plot purchased by the complainant from one Prem Sukh S/o Har Chand on 09.11.1994 and business of auto parts was started in the name of M/s Ganesh Industrial Corporation. The (3 of 5) [ CRLMP-1826/2013] allegation was that petitioner No.1 prepared a forged gift deed and using the same patta was obtained. The preparation of forged documents was also one of the allegations.
texts.arguments: 4. Counsel for the petitioners argued both the cases together and tried to make out the case that both the FIRs were having facts akin to each other and the core issues of the complaint were same. It is also argued that the matter was part of the dispute which was subjudice before this Court in S.B. Civil Writ Petition No.10412/2011 whereby the patta in question is being adjudicated by this Court while maintaining the status quo. As per counsel for the petitioner, the dispute involved was of civil rights which were also under adjudication and all the three consecutive FIRs contained the given question of the property in question and therefore, were repetition of allegations and counsel for the petitioner particularly harped upon the order passed by the competent Court in criminal case No. 219/2011 on 03.05.2014 whereby the learned trial court has acquitted the petitioner of the allegations under Section 420, 467, 468 & 471 of IPC giving the benefit of doubt while noting the fact that the patta in question was found to be correct by the Board of Revenue. 5. Learned Public Prosecutor has submitted factual report in both the misc. petitions and has also argued that the allegations in the FIR are different as in the first case while discharging the duties of the helper, the petitioners have prepared a forged gift deed by the forged signatures of the petitioner and the same resulted into issuance of the patta. It is contended that the (4 of 5) [ CRLMP-1826/2013] machines were also established by the complainant and efforts were being made by the accused persons who wanted to control and dispose of those machines. The refusal of those machines which were categorically owned by the complainant has resulted into such criminal prosecution. It is also contended that on the basis of prima facie evidence gathered including the documents, FSL report and statement of certain witnesses, the prima facie offence was separately made out against the petitioner. It is also stated from the FSL report that the disputed signatures stamped and marked as Q-2, the FSL report also pointed out that the stamped and marked dispute signatures on the laminated note sheet on 02.01.1999 also enclosed in the record did not match the signatures and the signatures were found to be forged in the report of the FSL. Manohar Lal & Anr vs State & Anr on 17 May, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85021612/ 2 6. The learned Public Prosecutor further stated that in criminal misc. petition No.1826/2013, the same pertains to stealing of certain documents pertaining to the machines and matching of signatures of Ram Dayal during investigation, the Provisional Registration Certificate issued by the District Industrial Officer including the form B Certificate of Registration and affidavit of Rajasthan Finance Corporation, the electricity bills and NOC issued by the Municipal Corporation on 11.06.1986 regarding the machines in question were taken on record and the conclusion of the investigation on these counts were complete and prima facie offence has been made out against Manohar Lal and Dharmendra under Section 379, 406, 467, 468, 471 & 120-B of IPC. 8. At this stage, learned counsel for the petitioner further submitted that the petitioner No.2 at the time of so called commission of offence was only 7 years, his date of birth reflected the date as 28.02.1992
